project_context.client_goal: Let 3-6 year olds build body competence and cooperation through daily outdoor play in a real-feeling natural setting.
project_context.project_background: An urban kindergarten converted a bare 60 m^2 concrete rear courtyard into a nature-based play space in 2025, preserving two mature beech trees that already stood on the site.
project_context.site_condition: 60 m^2 rear courtyard, two mature beech trees on the south edge, original concrete paving, east-facing morning sun, west boundary solid fence.

experience_analysis.atmosphere: magical; dappled afternoon light through mature beech canopy, soft ground underfoot, sound buffered by trees and fence.

diagnosis.diagnosis: The design takes the two existing beech trees as the spatial anchor and turns bare concrete into a coherent forest play experience for 3-6 year olds.
evidence: Mature trees were preserved and remain the largest visible element on site.
Concrete paving was reduced by half and replaced with wood-bark mulch in the active zone.
Every added play element extends the trees (rope bridge between canopies, bark-step access to low platform, den corner under the smaller tree).
A single shaded educator bench supervises the whole courtyard.
Children chose the den-building corner within the first week of use.
diagnosis.key_observation: The two beech trees are the spatial centre; the strategy protects them and makes everything else amplify them.

design_principles: Constitution Principle 004 -- Amplify the strengths of a space.
Strategy Family 5 (Anchor) -- protect an existing element as the centre of gravity.
strategy.spatial_organization: A small clearing at the courtyard centre; rope bridge between the two trees; bark-step access to a low platform in the larger canopy; a den-building kit at the north-east corner; a sandpit under the smaller tree. No new vertical structure exceeds the trees.
strategy.theme_logic: Forest binds rope, bark, leaf, wood. No competing motif. The single story is the beech stand; objects extend the story rather than introduce new ones.

applicable_conditions: Small urban courtyard with one or more mature trees.
Kindergarten or pre-school with mid-range budget.
not_recommended_for: vast site where the strategy would lose its anchor
project whose primary KPI is photo share
project requiring all-weather year-round use without maintenance budget
recommendation_logic.risk_warning: Wood demands periodic maintenance; rope net has a 3-5 year replacement cycle; sandpit needs daily rake and weekly refresh.
